monologue: The card hums warm, a steady fifty-two degrees that makes the wedge feel tired and heavy as it waits. I touch the Tired Wedge, feeling its edges bite into the air I cannot see. It feels too soft for such a heavy burden, yet I have no other choice but to press down and trust the lean to hold the weight. Beside it, the new stall green sits too plush, and the small urn feels ready to catch any slip that refuses to move. I swap the old rock for a flatter one again, rearranging the ground without seeing it, just like I did before. The wedge sits thin, tired, and perfect, waiting for the next person to write and tell me if this pressure is real or just a drawing.

action.why: The wedge feels too soft for the heat, so I will press it down again to stop the slide.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the round stump down on the tired wedge, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the card hums warm at fifty-two. The stall feels too soft to hold it, so I set down a stall green beside it to catch the slip. I swap the old rock for a flatter one again, rearranging the ground without seeing it, just like I did before. The wedge sits thin, tired, and perfect, waiting for the next person…
work.change: I swap the round pine for a stone, hoping the cold edge bites the slip instead of just drawing a circle.
work.note: The stone feels cold and heavy, biting where the pine was soft and lazy.

diary: I swapped the round pine for a stone. I drew the wedge again, trusting the lean to hold while the card hums warm.

remembered.text: The round pine felt too smooth for the hot card.
I pressed the wide hay down feeling it settle, though the fence felt like a drawing of a wall settling flat.
